Collab.description:
Collaborative `.md` editing over Yjs. Two frame families ride the same channel:

  * **JSON-RPC control plane** (`rt.subscribe` / `rt.unsubscribe` / `rt.collab_flush`) — same text-frame shape as every other channel.
  * **Binary data plane** — Yjs sync protocol as raw bytes: `[1 byte kind][16 bytes file_id BE][payload]`. Kinds: `0x01` UPDATE (Yjs update blob), `0x02` AWARENESS (presence, not persisted), `0x03` SYNC (state vector c→s / diff s→c).

AuthZ: `Read` on the file for subscribe (JSON) and for `0x03 SYNC` (defense-in-depth vs the subscribe gate). `Update` on the file for `0x01 UPDATE` and `rt.collab_flush`. AWARENESS is presence-only and rides the subscribe-time Read gate.

See `docs/plan/markdown-collab.md` and `src/application/services/collab_wire.rs`.

Folder.description: A folder's mutation stream — file/subfolder created events fire here. AuthZ: caller must hold `Read` on the folder.

Job.description: A named background job's run lifecycle — Started / Progress / Ended. Consumed by the admin dashboard so operators who trigger a long-running job (backend migration, thumb import…) can navigate off the admin page and come back without losing progress. AuthZ: admin-only (Class 3 role-scoped) — non-admin gets `topic_forbidden`, indistinguishable on the wire from an unknown topic.

UserAuthz.description: A user's private AuthZ-change channel. Identity-scoped: caller_id must equal userId (no admin bypass).

userId.description: User UUID — must match the authenticated caller

UserNotifications.description: A user's private notifications channel. Identity-scoped: caller_id must equal userId (no admin bypass). Auto-subscribed at session open; the FE bell refetches `GET /api/notifications` when a `notification_received` event fires. The DB row is authoritative — a missed push recovers on the next mount.

userId.description: User UUID — must match the authenticated caller

collab_binary_frame_schema.description: Raw bytes of a collab wire frame. Layout: `[1 byte kind][16 bytes file_id BE][payload...]`. `kind`: `0x01` UPDATE (Yjs update blob), `0x02` AWARENESS (opaque presence bytes, not persisted), `0x03` SYNC (Yjs state vector c→s / Yjs update s→c). `file_id` is a UUID serialised as its 16 raw bytes (matches `Uuid::as_bytes()` on the server; `y-codemirror.next` binary handling on the client). Empty payloads are legal only for the SYNC direction that carries a state vector of zero clients — Yjs encodes that as a single `0x00` byte, NOT zero bytes.

flushed.description: `true` when a blob write happened; `false` when the CRDT text was unchanged since the last flush (short-circuit).

CollabBinaryFrame.description: Raw bytes of a collab wire frame. Layout: `[1 byte kind][16 bytes file_id BE][payload...]`. `kind`: `0x01` UPDATE (Yjs update blob), `0x02` AWARENESS (opaque presence bytes, not persisted), `0x03` SYNC (Yjs state vector c→s / Yjs update s→c). `file_id` is a UUID serialised as its 16 raw bytes (matches `Uuid::as_bytes()` on the server; `y-codemirror.next` binary handling on the client). Empty payloads are legal only for the SYNC direction that carries a state vector of zero clients — Yjs encodes that as a single `0x00` byte, NOT zero bytes.

FileDeletedData.description: The wire doesn't distinguish soft (trash) vs. permanent delete — clients treat both as "disappears from the folder view". `parent_id` is the folder the file used to live in.

FileMovedData.description: Emitted on BOTH the source (`from`) and destination (`to`) folder topics. Subscribers to either see the event exactly once because they're subscribed to only one of the two.

FolderDeletedData.description: Soft vs. permanent delete are indistinguishable on the wire.

FolderMovedData.description: Emitted on BOTH the source (`from`) and destination (`to`) folder topics — same shape as `FileMoved`.

JobRunEndedData.description: A background job's run ended. `success = true` for a normal completion; `false` for failure / timeout / cancelled / paused-with-unhandled-outcome. `reason` populates the toast text on the `false` branch and links to `/admin/jobs/<name>` for the full outcome. Consumer typically drops its subscription on receipt (job is done).

JobRunProgressData.description: A background job made progress. Throttled at the publish site to at most one per 3 s per job (see scheduler engine). `step` / `total` populate a progress bar; all three fields are optional because different jobs report different granularities.

JobRunStartedData.description: A background job's run started. `name` matches the scheduler-registered job name (e.g. `backend_migration`). `actor` is `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` today — the scheduler doesn't yet thread the trigger caller through.

NotificationReceivedData.description: A new notification was created for the caller. Pure cache-invalidation event — no fields on the wire. The FE refetches `GET /api/notifications` on receipt and reads the payload from the REST DTO (see `openapi.json`). Zero schema overlap between the bus wire (this file) and the REST wire — the strict form of the AsyncAPI-defines-envelope / OpenAPI-defines-payload split.

flushed.description: `true` when a blob write happened; `false` when the CRDT text was unchanged since the last flush (short-circuit).

RtErrorCode.description:
Stable integer error code. Values are frozen across releases — a new denial cause gets a new value, never repurposes an existing one. Application-defined codes (-32099..=-32000):
· -32001 NO_READ — resource-scoped topic, caller lacks Read (or resource doesn't exist — indistinguishable by design)
· -32002 NO_SHARE — resource requires Share, caller has Read but not Share
· -32003 NO_COMMENT — resource requires Comment
· -32004 TOPIC_FORBIDDEN — identity-scoped mismatch or unknown/malformed topic
· -32005 SUB_LIMIT — per-connection subscription cap hit
· -32006 RATE_LIMITED — subscribe-frame token bucket exhausted
· -32007 NO_EDIT — CRDT edit frame from a caller without Edit
Standard JSON-RPC 2.0 codes:
· -32603 INTERNAL_ERROR · -32600 INVALID_REQUEST · -32601 METHOD_NOT_FOUND · -32602 INVALID_PARAMS

RtErrorMessage.description: Stable wire vocabulary; matches the corresponding `code`.

RtErrorObject.description: JSON-RPC 2.0 error object. `code` + `message` form a stable pair; `data` optionally carries caller-visible context (e.g. offending topic).

data.description: Optional caller-facing context; shape depends on the specific `code`.

RtEventDataUnion.description: Tagged union of every possible `rt.event` payload. Discriminated by the sibling `event` field (see `RtEventKind`).

RtEventKind.description: Discriminator for the `data` payload. Mirrors the `#[serde(tag = "event", rename_all = "snake_case")]` variants of the Rust `MessageBusEvent` enum — a new event kind is a new enum variant on both sides.

RtRevokedReason.description: Server-side eviction cause. Stable vocabulary; a new eviction reason is a new enum value.

result.description: Method-specific result payload. See the concrete response schema for each `method`.

bearerAuth.description: OxiCloud JWT — same access_token minted by `POST /api/auth/login` (or the OPAQUE handshake). Programmatic clients set `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` on the WS upgrade request. DPoP-bound tokens are refused on this path (the WS handshake cannot carry a DPoP proof); browsers use `ticketAuth` instead.

ticketAuth.description: Browser path — the FE first calls `POST /api/rt/ticket` under the full REST middleware stack (auth + DPoP-proofed request), receives an opaque one-shot UUID with a 30 s TTL, then sets `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: oxi.ticket.<uuid>` on the WS upgrade. The server redeems the ticket (single-use — a second attempt fails) and treats the WS session as authenticated for the caller who issued it. See `docs/architecture/message-bus-and-notifications.md § F` and `handlers/rt_ticket_handler.rs`.
ticketAuth.name: Sec-WebSocket-Protocol

collabFlush.summary: **`rt.collab_flush`** → the FE editor's explicit-save path. Server checks `Permission::Update` on the file, calls `CollabSession::flush_to_blob` (idempotent, short-circuits on unchanged content hash), returns `{ flushed: bool }`. Denials use `no_edit`. See `src/interfaces/api/handlers/rt_ws.rs::handle_collab_flush`.
collabFlush.title: rt.collab_flush — force flush CRDT text to blob (on tab close / save)

ping.summary: **`rt.ping`** → application-level liveness probe. Reply is `rt.pong` with `result.pong = true`. Distinct from RFC 6455 transport-level Ping; useful when a proxy black-holes traffic without dropping the socket.
ping.title: rt.ping — application-level keepalive

receiveCollabAwareness.summary: Server broadcasts another editor's presence bytes. Fan-out policy is same as UPDATE — every subscriber including origin.
receiveCollabAwareness.title: 0x02 AWARENESS (s→c) — peer presence

receiveCollabRevoked.summary: Grant revoked, file deleted, or admin kicked. Client tears down the editor UI.
receiveCollabRevoked.title: rt.revoked — collab session evicted

receiveCollabUpdate.summary: Server broadcasts a Yjs update it applied for another editor on the same file. The originating client also receives its own update back — Yjs's `applyUpdate` is idempotent so this is a no-op locally.
receiveCollabUpdate.title: 0x01 UPDATE (s→c) — fan-out from another editor

receiveFolderEvent.summary: **`rt.event`** → server pushes a mutation notice (file/subfolder created, renamed, deleted). Client updates its live view. Delivered only to subscribers holding `Read` on the folder.
receiveFolderEvent.title: rt.event — folder mutation notification

receiveRevoked.summary: **`rt.revoked`** → server evicts the client's subscription (grant revoked, resource deleted, session expired). Client stops rendering the topic and drops any local state.
receiveRevoked.title: rt.revoked — subscription evicted

sendCollabAwareness.summary: Presence-only (cursor position, user handle, colour). Not applied to the CRDT, not persisted. AuthZ: the subscribe-time Read gate is sufficient — a Viewer's cursor is legitimate.
sendCollabAwareness.title: 0x02 AWARENESS (c→s) — presence / cursor position

sendCollabSync.summary: Client sends its Yjs state vector so the server can compute the diff needed to catch it up. Payload is `Y.encodeStateVector(doc)` bytes; the empty state vector is a single `0x00` byte (varint 0 clients) — NOT zero-length. Server replies with a `0x03 SYNC` frame carrying the Yjs update bytes.
sendCollabSync.title: 0x03 SYNC (c→s, sync-step-1) — send client state vector

sendCollabUpdate.summary: Client emits a Yjs update blob describing local edits. Server applies to the per-file actor's `yrs::Doc`, broadcasts to every other subscribed socket on the same file, and arms the debouncer for eventual flush-to-blob. AuthZ: server checks `Permission::Update` per frame — a Viewer's frame gets `collab.write_denied` audit and the socket closes.
sendCollabUpdate.title: 0x01 UPDATE (c→s) — apply Yjs update to the shared doc

subscribeCollab.summary: Subscribe to a file's collab channel. Clears the server-side `Permission::Read` gate on the file so the binary data-plane frames start flowing. Without this, the server drops binary frames from this socket. Same JSON-RPC shape as the folder subscribe; only the topic prefix differs.
subscribeCollab.title: rt.subscribe — join a collab session (AuthZ gate: Read)

subscribeFolder.summary: **`rt.subscribe`** → client joins a folder's mutation stream. Reply is `rt.subscribed` (ok) or `rt.error` (permission denied, unknown topic, etc.).
subscribeFolder.title: rt.subscribe — join a folder's mutation stream

unsubscribeFolder.summary: **`rt.unsubscribe`** → client leaves a previously-joined folder. Server acks with `rt.subscribed` (`result.ok = true`) — the ack message is shared with subscribe.
unsubscribeFolder.title: rt.unsubscribe — leave a folder's mutation stream
